author: Miri Teixeira
description:
Fields Of Mistria has plenty to keep you busy--from farming to friendship, mining to marriage--but it's also home to a few secrets and cheeky references. We've collated all the things you might have missed about the game, which features plenty of easily overlooked useful features, and options to make your life easier (or more interesting!). Like its contemporaries, Stardew Valley and Story Of Seasons, Fields Of Mistria has plenty of secrets lurking beneath the surface. 

This guide does include several spoilers relating to plot and unlockable skills,
title: Fields Of Mistria 1.0 – Secrets And Easter Eggs

author: Miri Teixeira
description:
Every NPC in Fields Of Mistria loves to receive gifts, but they can be pretty picky about which ones come their way. In general, gifts fall into six categories, and your friendship will improve (or stagnate) depending on how well you're attuned to your friends' preferences. Getting gifts right can also lead to romance, so keep our guide handy when you're exploring Fields Of Mistria's many romance and marriage options. This updated gift guide has all you need to know about gifting, including what gifts to get the new 1.0 vendor NPCs and who to give the newly introduced items to.

THIS GUIDE CONTAINS SPOILERS FOR FIELDS OF MISTRIA 1.0 UNLOCKABLE CHARACTERS AND ITEMS.
title: Fields Of Mistria 1.0 – Gift Guide

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Pedro Pascal plays Joel in HBO's popular The Last of Us, based on the Naughty Dog game, and he has been praised for his performance. However, he wasn't the only actor in the mix for the role.

Oscar-winner Matthew McConaughey revealed more details on the Happy Sad Confused podcast about why he didn't star on the show. The Last of Us "was really good but it wasn't for me at the time," the actor said.

He added that signing on to The Last of Us would have also meant committing himself to the project for potentially years on end. "In success, this is something you'll be doing for years and years and years," he said. At the time he was circling The Last of Us, McConaughey said he "wasn't really acting" and was focusing more on writing and leadership roles in fil
title: Matthew McConaughey Discusses Passing On Playing Joel In The Last Of Us Show

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Remakes and remasters are popular, but Benson Russell, a designer on Uncharted: Drake's Fortune at Naughty Dog, has said he's not interested in a new one for the 2007 game.

Speaking to FRVR, Russell said he's not against the idea of remakes and remasters generally, but he said Uncharted is "still in the zeitgeist" and available on modern platforms. "What's the point of remastering [or remaking] it?" he said.

Instead of a remake or a remaster, Russell said a better idea might be to do what fans have been clamoring for: make a new one. “Take the lessons of Uncharted 4 and make a new game ..." he said.
title: Former Uncharted Dev On Possible New Remake Or Remaster: “What’s The Point?”

author: Cameron Koch
description:
Wardogs, an upcoming large-scale, hardcore FPS inspired by games like Arma, is taking a unique approach with its marketing by listing 10 reasons why prospective players shouldn't buy it.

In an official video, developer Bulkhead revealed September 10 as Wardogs' Steam early access release date, but also laid the rest of its cards on the table. Point by point, it outlined all the main reasons why potential players might not want to take a chance on the shooter, ranging from its lack of content, high early-access price, visual fidelity, and even the failure of Bulkhead's previous shooter, Battalion: 1944. 

"Before the hype train gets out of control, we want to do something most AAA marketing teams would
title: Shooter Climbing Steam Charts Lists 10 Reasons Not To Buy It

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
A week has passed since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls launched for PC and PS5, and the new fighting game is off to a solid start. According to new estimates by Alinea Analytics, the game has reportedly sold 485,000 units as of August 12, with PS5 being the dominant platform.

As outlined by Alinea Analytics’ head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, the PS5 accounted for 74% of sales, and Steam 26%. That's not too surprising, as the game experienced technical issues on PC. Developer Arc System Works released a patch
title: Marvel Tokon Nears 500K Sales In Its First Week Despite Fighting Games’ Niche Appeal

author: Jason Fanelli
description:
For many fighting game fans, It's impossible to look at Marvel Tokon and not think of Marvel Vs. Capcom. 

The crossover series defined the crossover tag genre, from X-Men Vs. Street Fighter in 1996 to Ultimate Marvel Vs. Capcom 3 in 2011. For some who didn't read comics as a kid, myself included, these games were the introduction to the X-Men, Avengers, and other Marvel faces that fought alongside Capcom's top characters.

With MvC dormant outside of a recent collection, Arc System Works has swooped in with Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, its own take on the Marvel tag fighter idea. The result is a wonderful fighting system and flashy new look that quickly establishes its own identity, one that is worthy of standing with the giants of the past--although the PC version isn't as super as the heroes in the game.

Fantastic four
title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Raises The Bar For Tag Fighters

author: Jordan Ramée
description:
Look, it's no surprise to anyone for me to admit that I like South of Midnight. I've written about it being a love letter to the American Deep South, noted how it was one of the best Xbox games of 2025, and talked about how much the game's story, characters, and setting have meant to me on video podcasts for both GameSpot and IGN. I want everyone to play this game, and there's never been a better time to do so on Steam.

As noticed by
title: Ignore Your Growing Backlog–It’s Time To Play South Of Midnight On Steam

author: S.E. Doster
description:
Season 5 Reloaded arrives in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 and Warzone later this month, and Activision has now revealed all of the details for this midseason update. Season 5 Reloaded adds a new weapon, additional multiplayer maps, and the final round-based Zombies map of the Black Ops 7 storyline.

Call of Duty Season 5 Reloaded start times

The Season 5 Reloaded update for Black Ops 7 and Warzone arrives on August 20. Call of Duty updates typically go live at 9 AM PT / 12 PM ET / 5 PM BST across all platforms.

This midseason update arrives only one day before the first Modern Warfare 4 beta begins. For those interested in trying this year's upcoming Call of Duty, the full MW4 beta dates
title: CoD: Black Ops 7 And Warzone Season 5 Reloaded Release Date And Details

author: Steve Watts
description:
The "fine, I'll just do it myself" approach has served indie developers well, capitalizing on the hunger for games that emulate beloved classics. Indie metroidvania games, boomer shooters, and retro-style platformers all owe their rise to the same trend of homage for underserved genres. Wild Blue Skies isn't the first game that aims to fill a Star Fox-shaped hole in gamers' hearts, but it is the one that feels most like pure homage. It could practically be an expansion.

Wild Blue Skies follows the formula set by Star Fox 64 incredibly closely, down to even specific details like including alternate paths through the map, all-range mode stages, and a rival company of evil pilots who hound you throughout the story campaign. The very first alternate path is revealed by one of your copilots challenging you to follow them around tricky obstacles, just like Falco in SF64. Even the world map forms a similarly tilted oblong ova
title: Wild Blue Skies Is Star Fox For Experts

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Unlike its work on the Spider-Man games, Insomniac won't be throwing players into an open-world environment with Marvel's Wolverine. It's an old-school single-player game that focuses on pushing the story from Point A to Point B, but that doesn't mean that you can't take a detour or two. This will allow players to spend some extra time with Logan, as Insomniac says that players can hunt down resources for new suits and take part in combat trials that'll test their skills.

"It is a story-driven adventure," senior project director Jess Reiner-Reed said to
title: Marvel’s Wolverine Has You Hunting For Resources, Drinking Whiskey, And Beating Up Nightmares

author: Eddie Makuch
description: GTA 6 preorders began in late June, and, as expected, there was enormous demand for the game. Take-Two said GTA 6 had unprecedented preorder numbers, but the company is not disclosing a specific figure to avoid
title: GTA 6 Preorders Alone Could Pay For Production Budget – Expert

author: Evan Campbell
description:
Starting next week, it's going to be totally acceptable to eat Pokemon. That's because Krispy Kreme on August 18 will launch a limited-time Pokemon Doughnut Collection, featuring tasty-looking pastries based on five beloved pocket monsters. 

You can take a bite of a Pikachu doughnut, filled with lemon creme and topped with "electrifying drizzle" as well as a Pikachu piece. Meanwhile, there's a Charmander doughnut containing a chocolate and toasted marshmallow filling. Other options include original glazed doughnuts but customized for Bulbasaur, Squirtle, Jigglypuff, and even the Poke Ball. A special-edition dozen looks to retail for about $21 in the US.
title: New Krispy Kreme Pokemon Doughnuts Announced, And You’re Gonna Wanna Eat ‘Em All

author: Mark Delaney
description:
Revealed during PlayStation's State of Play earlier this year, The Lost Wild is a first-person horror game that combines the awe of walking amongst dinosaurs, such as in Jurassic Park, with the terror of being hunted by a creature you can't defeat, à la Alien: Isolation. For Great Ape Games CEO Nick Gregory, it's a lot more than that; it's the culmination of an idea he's had in his mind since childhood. 

GameSpot recently caught up with Gregory via email to discuss the more than 20-year journey from boyhood dream to a Steam wishlist darling. He spoke to his team's growth as the project shifted to a full-time job, The Lost Wild's humble origins before he even knew how to really make games, and the subtleties of depicting dinosaurs as "animals, not monsters."

GameSpot: As I unde
title: Jurassic Park Meets Alien In This Childhood Dream Turned Horror Game

author: Callum Self
description:
Expedition 33 blew me away. I’m not alone in that--in fact, it’s the overwhelming consensus. Sandfall Interactive’s debut game combines a heartfelt narrative, a unique twist on turn-based RPG combat, and a world that’s as thematic as it is beautiful into one outstanding experience. It was my Game of the Year for 2025, and now you can grab it at its lowest price yet.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the best RPGs I’ve ever played. Sure, there will always be people who don’t enjoy it, but its widespread acclaim speaks for itself. As someone who doesn’t usually play many games in the genre beyond older Final Fantasy entries and Atlus RPGs, Expedition 33 feels like decades of role-playing game design refined into one essential adventure.

The o
title: Masterpiece RPG Expedition 33 Is Cheaper Than Ever Right Now, But Only For 24 Hours

author: Ben Janca
description:
Tam played a couple of hours of Wolverine and was shocked to see just how much of what I experienced lines up with the current X-Men media landscape.

Wolverine takes place on Earth-1048--the same universe as Insomniac's Spider-Man games--and opens with an assault on a Weapon X base, where Wolverine teams up with his longtime hater Sabertooth. I played through this just days after watching them both do the same thing in X-Men '97.

A foolhardy mission featuring Wolverine is a pretty common narrative beat in Logan's story, irrespective of format, but that sense of fortuitously timed familiarity became a feeling that permeated much of what I saw and played of Wolverine.
title: Wolverine Hands-On Preview Impressions

author: Tamoor Hussain
description:
It'd be inaccurate to say the X-Men are having a resurgence, given that the team's escapades are perennially popular stories in comics. However, between Marvel Tokon, Avengers: Doomsday, and X-Men '97, the X-Men are certainly having a pop-culture moment. Also in the zeitgeist mix is Marvel's Wolverine, a PlayStation 5-exclusive title developed by Insomniac Games.

I played a couple of hours of Wolverine and was shocked to see just how much of what I experienced lines up with the current X-Men media landscape. Wolverine takes place on Earth-1048--the same universe as Insomniac's Spider-Man games--and opens with an assault on a Weapon X base, where Wolverine teams up with his longtime hater Sabertooth. I played through this just days after watching them both do the same thing i
title: Wolverine Uses Blind Rage And Violence To Make Combat Feel Authentic

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
One of the best systems for getting your hands on rare Pokemon is set to close down in a few months, as Pokemon Bank will stop working next year. According to Serebii, the shutdown date has been penciled in for February 27, 2027.

This will effectively end the 3DS era of Pokemon, although the writing has been on the wall for a long time. Following the closure of the 3DS eShop in March 2023, 3DS owners were no longer able to download the app. Nintendo had already launched a replacement program for Switch, iOS, and Android a few years earlier, which served as a beefier upgrade when compared to Pokemon Bank.

The 3DS program still had value, as you could bring plenty of rare Pokemon from ol
title: Nintendo Is Pulling The Plug On One Of The Best Ways To Get Rare Pokemon

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Recently, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma saw a demo of The Elder Scrolls 6 and cryptically suggested the game's full name will have an eight-character subtitle.

That remains to be seen, but Elder Scrolls fans took the morsel of news and ran with it, offering many theories as to what the game could be called. One possibility is a reference found in Bethesda's last big game, Starfield.

Fans have suggested subtitles like Dominion, Starfall, Orsinium, Covenant
title: Elder Scrolls Fans Think They’ve Worked Out The Subtitle For Elder Scrolls 6

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced has been a welcome hit for Ubisoft, and several weeks after the game launched for PC and console, new stats about it have been revealed. Mind you, these stats lean toward more esoteric data points, so if you've been curious about which Caribbean couture has been the most popular or just how shattered Edward Kenway's back must be after doing a dangerous amount of crouching, then these infographics are for you.

Kicking things off with a look at Kenway's threads. Ubisoft revealed that the subdued greys of the Privateer outfit is the most popular with players so far. Kenway's ship, the Jackdaw, has also traveled over 40 million kilometers thanks to the collective efforts of players, a distance that equates to 1,000 trips around the world at full sail. When it comes to weapons, Le Bourgeys Blades are the favorite of many a swashbuckler, and players have a 47% win rate against Legendary-c
title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced Players Are Absolutely Destroying Edward Kenway’s Back

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
The Amazon-owned streaming site Twitch is now using channels to train generative AI systems, and the company's top product boss knows it's a controversial piece of news that most people won't like.

By default, Twitch channels are now used to train generative AI models across Amazon, and users need to opt-out. Opting-out isn't enough, though, as any chats on a channel that hasn't opted out will still be used for training.

During a livestream, Twitch chief product officer Mike Minton said that if the model training was on an opt-in basis, no one would do it.
title: Twitch Is Now Using Channels To Train Generative AI, And The Company Knows It’s Unpopular

author: Steve Watts
description:
Fire Emblem has always been known for its mechanical density and complexity, but Fortune's Weave applies a force multiplier. With an array of four differentiated but intertwining story campaigns, it feels complex in a way that could prove overwhelming. Having played the first several chapters of two of the campaigns, each had its own wrinkles and elements that could have supported their own standalone campaigns--all composing a sprawling narrative that appears to reward exploring it in full to see every scene and interaction. 

Fortune's Weave looks to be a conscious effort to restore some of the magic of Three Houses, following the more divisive Fire Emblem Engage. That means a tale that is more grand and sweeping across multiple factions, including a time-jump element that Nintendo revealed during its recent Direct presentation. At its core, though, this is a story that focuses on four main protagonists, the so-c
title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave Feels Like Four Games’ Worth Of Fire Emblem

author: Steve Watts
description: With four campaigns that each have multiple systems of their own, Fortune's Weave may be the most ambitious Fire Emblem to date.
title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave Feels Like Four Games’ Worth Of Fire Emblem – Preview

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Video games don't typically reference current affairs, but a new Genshin Impact update seems to be poking fun at the recent Washington Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool debacle. Players have discovered a document in the game, penned by "Grand Duke Diomid Turzov," that goes into detail--and with strange grammatical choices--about a fountain that was "ruined" by shoddy workmanship and vandals. As Turzov explained, he's looking for a few good guards to help ensure that the renovation project continues without any additional complications.

"I built a fountain. It is enormous. Without question, it is the most beautiful fountain in all of Snezhnaya," the note reads (via
title: Genshin Impact’s New Update Appears To Mock The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool Fiasco

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Hot Toys has made plenty of video game figures over the years--from Batman: Arkham Knight to Marvel's Spider-Man--but it's finally venturing into the world of Fortnite. The collectible toys manufacturer has shown off its first-ever sixth-scale figure based on the popular battle royale game, with the dimension-hopping everyman Jonesy in the spotlight.

Limited to 3,000 units, the Hot Toys Jonesy figure is designed to look just like the character's in-game model. Hot Toys has replicated the art direction of Fortnite for this figure--blending stylized realism with cartoonish proportions--and the collectible features soft silicone arms, a fabric tactical outfit, and various accessories. The clothing details include a scarf, a vest with a harness, belts, camouflage pants with stitched patch details, and intricate extras like a metal mat
title: Fortnite’s Jonesy Looks Weirdly Real In His First Hot Toys Figure
